title: Differences in soloing and Armstrong as neither Western nor Dixieland
summary: Clayton contrasts New York trumpeters like Taft Jordan with Western players and says Armstrong fit no category.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: There's a difference in a New York trumpet player's solo and a soloist from Kansas City or Omaha. And two good examples of that was Taft Jordan and Shad Collins. To me they played like all the trumpet players played in New York, the style. And we even, take little Taft Smith, we had a different kind of approach to playing a solo.
And sometimes when Shad was in our band he would play like Taft Jordan who was with .........
That's hard to explain, but I can quite, I can see what you mean and you can actually hear.
It's a different way, a different approach. But you see, that's what made
Louis to me, so great. He didn't play like any of them. He didn't play Western, he didn't play Eastern. He just played like Louis. And it all came out .........
: Yes, and he didn't really play like a ......
He wasn't a Dixie Land player, because everybody wants, all the guys would like to say Louis, just because he came from New Orleans.
But he wasn't, not a Dixie-Land player.
: No, even if you compare him with King Oliver who was excellent........
: .........musician, Louis had a ....... It's very extraordinary where that came from.
